blocks.t: STEREO NOT UTILIZED ON DEDICATED UPRITES
Konami introduces stereo sound. Please read instructions carefully. If your video cabinet doesn’t utilize two speakers, follow instructions for mono output.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION HOW TO CHANGE TO MONAURAL/STEREO

Adjusting Sound Volume In stereo specifications, adjust volume of each speaker separately (L and R). In monaural specifications, use R-volume switch to adjust volume. L-volume switch is irrelevant to volume. By R VOLUME.

If your cabinet has two speaker wire speakers as above, disregard mono outputs shown to the right &— Move the Jumper Wire to Appropriate Connector *Note: Mono & Stereo sound cannot operate simultaneously. For Mono Sound Use pin #10 and L of the 56 pin edge connector to the speaker contacts. Also connect Jumper connector into CN4. For Stereo Sound Use connector CN6 as your speaker output ports connect pins 1 & 2 to the left speaker pins 3 & 4 to the right speakers. Also connect Jumper connector to CN5.
Use Pin 10 &L For Mono Sound (one speaker)

Punkshot requires horizontally mounted monitor. It also generates composite negative sync. If your monitor is composite positive sync, you will have to change to composite negative sync.
To alternate composite positive sync to composite negative sync, use 7404 IC or 74LS04 IC. The signal on the output pin from the PC.B. is a combination of H-sync and V-sync.
NEGATIVE COMPOSITE SYNC. OUTPUT TO MONITOR (PIN P on P.C.B. EDGE) POSITIVE COMPOSITE SYNC. (+5V and GND should be taken out of the PC. Board.)

No Sound 1). Check +12V line at the PC.B. 2). Make sure both speaker out wires are connected to the speakers. (DO NOT CONNECT A GROUND.)

/O Problem (coin 1 1). Do not hook a coin counter to the coin 1 or coin 2 outputs. This doesn’t work or Joystick will cause damage. Up doesn’t work, etc.) 2). Check your schematic for the 74LS253 IC that corresponds to your VO problem. Check the appropriate pin with a scope or multimeter for a high output (5V), if output is low replace the 74LS253.
DO NOT WIRE COIN COUNTERS TO THE COIN 1 OR COIN 2 OUTPUTS. THIS WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE I/O MICROCHIP 74LS253. COIN COUNTERS CAN ONLY BE WIRED TO COIN COUNTER OUTPUTS.
